subject: Request: Allocation of uptime credits for 2026-01-05 edge failover
messages:
From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@tidalworks.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@tidalworks.com
Date: 2026-01-07T09:15:00-08:00
Subject: Request: Allocation of uptime credits for 2026-01-05 edge failover

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for taking this — we had a visible impact to a subset of our traffic on 2026-01-05 between ~02:10–03:05 UTC when our front-door failed over to the secondary edge. Our monitoring shows increased 5xxs and 150–300ms latency spikes for about 45 minutes for ~12% of requests. Per our contract we expect uptime accounting to exclude customer-originated or CDN failovers, but Redwood’s status page lists this as a service degradation (partial) rather than a third-party CDN event.

We’re asking for clarification on how Redwood apportions uptime credits in mixed incidents where a third-party CDN failover triggered transient routing through your edge and resulted in partial degradation. If Redwood is counting this against our SLA window, we’d like to request a credit for the impacted period. I’ve attached our incident timeline and a short log excerpt.

Can you confirm what evidence you need to evaluate this, and whether a credit is likely? Our renewal is coming up and we need this reconciled before we finalize terms.

Appreciate it —
Samantha Ortiz
Platform Reliability Lead
TidalWorks

Attachments: tidal-incident-timeline-20260105.pdf, edge-routing-trace-20260105.log

From: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
To: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@tidalworks.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-01-07T10:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: Allocation of uptime credits for 2026-01-05 edge failover

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear timeline and logs. I’m looping in Marissa (SRE) and Marcus (SLA ops) to run a quick correlation across our edge traces and the control plane routing decisions.

Quick asks so we don’t chase the wrong artifact:
- Can you confirm the public CDN provider that reported the failover and any support ticket IDs?
- Do you have client-side traces that show request paths that hit our origin vs bypassed caches?

I’ll prioritize this. If we determine the impact was caused primarily by an upstream CDN failover we will treat it as a third-party exception per section 4.2 of the SLA; if the degradation began inside our boundary (edge queuing, degraded host), we’ll apportion credits for the measured window of partial degradation. We aim to resolve within 48 hours.

— Rafael
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0182

From: marissa.cole@redwood.ai
To: rafael.mendes@redwood.ai, Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@tidalworks.com>
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.ai, diego.fernandez@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-01-08T14:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: Allocation of uptime credits for 2026-01-05 edge failover

Hi all — I pulled the edge trace and control plane logs for the window Samantha referenced. Summary of findings:  

- 02:07–02:12 UTC: multiple health-check flaps recorded for a subset of our edge nodes in us-west-2. Root cause appears to be a rapid reconfiguration from the CDN provider’s edge-to-origin routing (their ticket: CDN-4492).
- 02:12–02:55 UTC: traffic routed through a secondary egress path increased tail latency; we saw elevated queueing on two hosts for ~18 minutes (02:21–02:39 UTC) with increased 5xx retries.
- 02:39–03:05 UTC: our autoscaling removed the two problematic hosts; traffic normalized.

Interpretation: the initial disturbance was externally triggered by the CDN failover, but there is a measurable period (~18 minutes) during which internal queueing and retries contributed materially to failed/slow responses. Per our SLA apportionment methodology we attribute the CDN-triggered routing change as a third-party event for the initial 5 minutes, then classify the middle 18 minutes as partial degradation that is within Redwood’s control to mitigate.

Proposed remediation/credit: allocate uptime credit for the 18-minute partial degradation window. We will not credit the initial 5 minutes (CDN failover) or the final recovery minutes where autoscaling resolved the transient pressure. Total credit = pro-rated downtime equivalent of 18 minutes against the monthly uptime window.

I’ve attached the extracted edge trace and a short incident timeline PDF. If TidalWorks prefers we can run a joint correlation session (30 min) to walk the traces.

— Marissa Cole
SRE Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

Attachments: tidal-incident-timeline-20260105.pdf

From: Samantha Ortiz <samantha.ortiz@tidalworks.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rafael.mendes@redwood.ai
Cc: marcus.lin@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-01-09T17:32:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: Allocation of uptime credits for 2026-01-05 edge failover

Hi Marissa / Rafael — thanks for the quick analysis and for being transparent about the split. We appreciate the proposed 18-minute apportionment. A few follow-ups before we sign off:  

1) Can you provide the exact calculation you used to convert the 18-minute window into the pro-rated credit (percentage of monthly uptime / token). We need that spelled out for our procurement team.
2) We still want the joint correlation session — please propose 30-minute slots tomorrow.
3) Please confirm the incident will be excluded from our renewal health calculation once the credit is issued.

If we can get the math and a calendar invite, we’ll accept the proposed credit and proceed with the renewal paperwork.

Thanks —
Samantha
Platform Reliability Lead, TidalWorks
